subject.title: [Security] CSRF risk via dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback on network-exposed gateway (V-02)

question: Should OpenClaw keep documented Host-header origin fallback as an operator-selected break-glass mode, or remove/harden it for network-exposed Gateway deployments?
rationale: The remaining work is a security-boundary and compatibility tradeoff, not a narrow confirmed bug fix: current behavior is intentional, documented, and audited, but still weakens origin hardening when enabled.

options.title: Harden fallback in place
options.body: Keep the documented flag but add defense-in-depth such as `Sec-Fetch-Site` or CSRF-token requirements, plus focused tests and docs for the accepted deployment model.

options.title: Remove fallback with migration
options.body: Delete the flag and provide upgrade guidance or doctor handling for users who relied on it for non-loopback Control UI access.

options.title: Accept current dangerous mode
options.body: Leave the flag as an explicit operator-selected downgrade and rely on current critical audit warnings plus explicit `allowedOrigins` guidance.

recommendation.title: Harden fallback in place
recommendation.body: Keep the documented flag but add defense-in-depth such as `Sec-Fetch-Site` or CSRF-token requirements, plus focused tests and docs for the accepted deployment model.

likelyOwner.reason: The earlier non-loopback-origin and loopback-fallback hardening history makes this the strongest available routing signal for the security/product decision.
